rubrics.evidence: Section 2 ranks applied NLP/LLM evaluation and adaptation first and efficient NLP/ML systems second, while marking pure ML theory “Not primary.” Section 1.1 emphasizes “datasets, baselines, ablations, evaluation frameworks, and reproducible systems.”
rubrics.reason: The direction ranking and final recommendation prioritize rigorous empirical research and systems implementation rather than theory-only specialization.

rubrics.evidence: Section 7 requires a replication-and-extension project with a “replication of one central result,” “at least two meaningful ablations,” error analysis, a technical report, and a clean public repository. Phases 2–3 schedule this artifact and a second research project.
rubrics.reason: Implementation, replication, independent exploration, and research artifacts form the preparation plan’s core deliverables and milestones; formal coursework is supporting preparation.

rubrics.evidence: Section 1.2 recommends efficient deep-learning systems because it “supports both research-scientist and ML-systems career paths.” Phase 5 requires checking “collaboration and internship evidence,” and Phase 8 evaluates student placements and internship policy.
rubrics.reason: Industry optionality affects topic prioritization, program investigation, internship preparation, and offer evaluation rather than appearing only as a general career aspiration.

rubrics.evidence: The bottom line targets “fully funded direct-entry programs” and funded research-master’s bridges while advising against substantial self-funding. Section 3.3 states that UK admission without funding “should be treated as a rejection unless separate funding is secured.” Section 10 requires written funding confirmation and an after-tax living-cost comparison.
rubrics.reason: Funding materially restricts eligible routes and acceptable offers. The report favors funded pathways over prestige-driven expenditure and operationalizes affordability through explicit acceptance rules.

rubrics.evidence: Section 2 compares directions by hands-on fit, preparation feasibility, industry value, and academic optionality; Section 4 compares regional structures and risks. Phase 5 says to “evaluate supervisors rather than ranking universities alone” and discard programs with only one plausible supervisor unless tied to an explicitly funded position. Phase 8 prioritizes adviser fit, funding, placements, resources, and internship policy.
rubrics.reason: The recommendation uses explicit comparative criteria, research evidence, outcomes, and practical trade-offs. These criteria change program eligibility and prioritization rather than relying primarily on institutional prestige.
